key_insight: Random Forest and XGBoost led shading-fault detection, but operating-condition differences limit conclusions about classifier superiority.
engineering_relevance: Reliable rooftop PV fault detection requires episode-aware validation and no-fault samples matched to fault operating conditions.
method: Benchmarked seven classifiers on real sensor data from a 4 kW rooftop PV plant with physically staged shading.
Used three repeats of five-fold group-aware nested cross-validation to keep episodes separate.
Applied SMOTE within training folds and Holm correction to pairwise statistical tests.
evidence_signal: Across 20,800 rows retaining all 17 fault episodes, Random Forest achieved 0.838 accuracy and 0.526 MCC, yet almost entirely missed four fault episodes.
watch_item: Clock time alone reached 0.44 MCC and PV-side voltage alone 0.72 MCC in post-hoc diagnostics, suggesting operating-condition confounding; matched no-fault sampling is needed before generalising rankings.
paper_title: Benchmarking Classical Machine Learning Models for Shading-Fault Detection in Rooftop Photovoltaic Systems Using Real Sensor Data
